high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 24: MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rates on July 24 reveals continued significant divergence across the Vietnamese banking system. The highest 12-month deposit rate currently stands at **7.8% p.a.** (ACB), with at least **7 banks** now offering 7.0% or above for 12-month tenors. ACB leads the market at 7.8% (12M), 7.7% (9M), and 7.6% (6M). Saigonbank follows at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1% for 12-month deposits. MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank all sit at 7.0% for 12-month tenors, with MBV and VCBNeo maintaining 7.0% flat across 6M, 9M, 12M, and 18M maturities.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 25 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: Vietnamese bank deposit rates continue to show significant divergence as of July 25, 2026, particularly across tenors of 6 months and above. The spread between the highest and lowest 12-month deposit rates among surveyed banks has widened to a notable 4.1 percentage points — ranging from a high of 7.8%/year down to 3.7%/year. ACB leads the market at 7.8%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank are clustered around the 7.0% mark for 12-month tenors. State-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) remain at the lower end of the spectrum.

high.title: VN-Index Loses Over 100 Points in One Week: What Awaits Investors?
high.summary:
Vietnam's equity market suffered one of its sharpest weekly corrections of 2026, with the VN-Index plunging over 100 points across the week to close at **1,686.1 points — down 101.3 points (-5.6%)**, marking the **fourth consecutive week of declines**. The most severe session was July 22nd, when the index shed more than 62 points in a single day, decisively breaking below the psychologically critical **1,700-point support level** amid broad-based selling across large-cap stocks, with many hitting their daily circuit-breaker limits. The HNX-Index also dropped 18.7 points (-6.4%) to 272.9. While bargain-hunting demand briefly emerged in the latter sessions, each recovery attempt stalled near 1,700 as sellers re-emerged. Notably, trading liquidity surged over 23% week-on-week, but this reflected forced selling and margin call activity rather than fresh capital inflows. **For bond and FX investors:** sustained equity weakness of this magnitude could accelerate foreign capital outflows, adding depreciation pressure on the VND. Monitor foreign net selling data and SBV FX intervention signals closely.

---

medium.title: First Bank to Report a Loss in Q2/2026
medium.summary:
Saigonbank (SGB), a small-tier Vietnamese commercial bank, became the first bank to report a net loss in Q2/2026. Net interest income — the bank's primary revenue source — collapsed 31.3% YoY to VND 160 billion, while total operating expenses rose 10.2% to VND 168.5 billion, pushing pre-provision profit down nearly 80%. Compounding the pressure, credit risk provisioning surged 62.4% to VND 63.7 billion. FX-related income (net FX trading gains) also fell sharply by 40.5% to just VND 2.5 billion, a minor but noteworthy signal of constrained trading activity. While SGB is a marginal player in the Vietnamese banking system and poses no systemic risk, its results are an early indicator of margin compression and rising asset quality stress that could be more broadly relevant if replicated at larger lenders. Fund managers should monitor upcoming Q2 earnings from systemically important banks (Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, Techcombank) for confirmation of sector-wide trends in NIM compression and provisioning cycles.

---

medium.title: State Bank of Vietnam Clarifies the 24-Hour Waiting Period for Online Transfers Exceeding VND 400 Million
medium.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued Official Dispatch No. 6190 to clarify its new regulation on large-value online payment transactions. Contrary to initial market concern, the mandatory **24-hour waiting period does NOT apply to all transfers above VND 400 million**. Instead, the delay applies only to transfers made to **new beneficiary accounts** or transactions that exceed a customer's self-registered transaction limit. Banks must implement the service — which allows customers to voluntarily set their own transaction limits and waiting periods — by **March 1, 2027**. The default threshold where the 24-hour hold is applied is VND 400 million, but only for customers who have not opted into a customized limit structure.

This regulation is primarily a **consumer financial security measure** targeting online fraud and scam transfers. For institutional market participants and fund managers, operational impact should be minimal given the customization options available. However, the move reflects the SBV's broader push to tighten payment system oversight, which is relevant context for banking sector regulatory risk assessments.

---

medium.title: For the First Time in 165 Days, Taiwan Fund Returns to Buy Vietnamese Stocks
medium.summary:
Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF — one of the largest foreign ETFs investing in Vietnamese equities with total AUM of approximately TWD 10.7 billion (~VND 8,700 billion) — recorded its first net inflow in 165 days during the July 23 session. The fund issued a net 2.5 million certificates, deploying roughly TWD 44 million (~VND 36 billion) into Vietnamese stocks. This is the first net buying session since February 9, 2026, following an extended period of either net redemptions or zero activity. While the inflow size is modest, the reversal in direction is notable given the sustained foreign outflow pressure facing Vietnam-focused ETFs over recent months. For VN-Index traders and foreign capital flow watchers, this could signal an early, tentative shift in sentiment among offshore institutional investors toward Vietnamese equities. It warrants close monitoring — a sustained pattern of inflows over subsequent sessions would carry considerably more weight than a single-day event. The broader context of foreign selling across Vietnamese equities (as evidenced by FPT and PNJ outflows noted below) suggests this single session should be treated cautiously rather than as a definitive trend reversal.

---

medium.title: Fundamentally Strong Stocks FPT, MWG, SSI All Down Double-Digits YTD — Experts Explain Why
medium.summary: A broad cohort of high-quality Vietnamese equities — including FPT, MWG (Mobile World), SSI, VJC, and MSN — have all declined by double digits year-to-date, with FPT retreating to its lowest price level in nearly three years (since November 2023). Market experts at FIDT attribute the selloff to a **valuation re-rating driven by the rising interest rate environment**: as the cost of capital increases, premium-valued growth stocks face disproportionately larger multiple compression, regardless of their underlying business quality. This dynamic is particularly relevant for fund managers holding Vietnamese equities, as it suggests the correction is **structural and rate-driven rather than idiosyncratic**, implying further downside risk if interest rates remain elevated. The expert commentary implies that the current rate environment is forcing a market-wide discount rate adjustment — a bearish signal for duration-sensitive assets including long-dated government bonds as well.

medium.title: Banking Sector Q2 2026 Financial Results Update (Morning of July 27): One Bank Reports a Loss
medium.summary: Q2 2026 earnings season is revealing significant stress in Vietnam's banking sector. **Saigonbank** reported a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026, a sharp reversal from a VND 76.4 billion profit in the same period last year; H1 2026 cumulative pre-tax profit fell **72.4% year-on-year to VND 48 billion**. **Eximbank** disclosed H1 2026 pre-tax profit of approximately VND 730 billion, down **51% year-on-year**, achieving only 48% of its full-year target. The breadth of banking sector earnings deterioration — spanning both smaller institutions like Saigonbank and mid-tier banks like Eximbank — points to rising credit costs, margin compression from the rate environment, and potentially worsening asset quality. This is a key watch item for Vietnamese government bond markets, as deteriorating bank profitability may reduce domestic institutional demand for bonds, and could increase pressure on the SBV to adjust policy rates.

medium.title: Multiple Corporate Executives Face Margin Calls as Stock Prices Plunge
medium.summary: Forced margin call selling (giải chấp) is accelerating across Vietnamese listed companies as the market continues to probe new lows. FPT Securities (FPTS) disclosed the forced sale of 128,400 TCM shares belonging to a board member of Thanh Cong Textile on July 24th, with TCM hitting its lowest price since November 2020. The wave of margin calls has spread to the real estate sector as well, with Hodeco (HDC) insiders also subject to forced share disposals. The emergence of widespread margin call activity is a significant systemic risk signal — it creates self-reinforcing downward price spirals, elevates market volatility, and historically has been associated with foreign investor risk-off positioning and VND liquidity tightening. This dynamic warrants close monitoring alongside SBV open market operations and interbank liquidity conditions.

medium.title: Should You Buy Certificates of Deposit for Higher Interest Rates?
medium.summary: This advisory piece from Banking Times explores the relative merits of bank-issued Certificates of Deposit (CDs) versus standard savings deposits in Vietnam. CDs offer potentially higher interest rates — particularly at longer tenors — reflecting banks' ongoing need to attract stable, longer-duration funding. However, the article cautions that higher rates come with trade-offs: CDs typically carry fixed terms with limited or no early redemption flexibility, and transferability is subject to the issuing bank's specific policies. The piece advises retail investors to align CD purchases with their liquidity planning horizon. For macro watchers, the continued promotion of higher-rate CDs signals that Vietnamese banks remain active in liability management and term-funding strategies. This is relevant in the context of the SBV's broader interest rate environment — if deposit rates at the CD level are being pushed higher to attract capital, this could foreshadow upward pressure on lending rates and influence the yield curve for short-to-medium tenor government bonds. Watch whether CD rates diverge further from the SBV's policy corridor.
